Thanks all — quick readout after checking our delivery logs and mail headers:

Root cause: the invite was generated for james+procure@auroralabs.com and delivered from portal@redwood-invite.com via a dedicated SES pool. DKIM and SPF are set correctly, but the email used the "Reply-To" header with the canonical portal subdomain which some enterprise MX rules treat as a forwarding vector and then enforce strict subaddressing rejection. In short, Aurora’s MX rejects incoming plus-addressed recipients from unauthenticated senders (their policy).

Mitigation we applied:
- Reissued a new invite to james@auroralabs.com (no plus addressing).
- Created a single-use activation link and posted it to the HubSpot deal (link is in the HubSpot note). We did not paste the link into email for audit reasons — James has access and can confirm receipt.
- Logged the event and attached the delivery headers excerpt to the deal for Aurora’s IT (invite-email-smtp-headers.txt).

Follow-ups:
- Karthik: confirm with James that he received the new invite at james@auroralabs.com; once accepted, please request the W-9 upload and mark onboarding stage as "portal-activated" in the deal.
- Marissa: consider adding a small UI checkbox on future invites: "Send to alias (plus-addressing)" with a warning about enterprise MX restrictions so AEs don’t default to plus-addresses.

James — apologies for the friction — we just resent. If you still don’t see it, please check with your IT that messages from portal@redwood-invite.com aren’t blackholed.

Regards,
Ben Carter
